Consult Summary:
26-year-old woman with 3-day history of worsening right-sided, predominantly periorbital, dull-to-sharp headache with photophobia and nausea; ibuprofen ineffective. Clinical impression of probable migraine; stronger analgesia and follow-up arranged.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute worsening headache, 3-day duration; constant baseline with intermittent exacerbations (8/10).
- Location: global but worse around right eye.
- Character: dull, occasionally sharp; gradual onset; worsening over 3 days.
- Associated positives: photophobia (“shooting lights,” light hurts), nausea (no vomiting), difficulty concentrating.
- Associated negatives: no visual loss/blurring, no neck stiffness, no focal weakness, no speech disturbance, no fever, no rash, no recent head injury.
- Triggers/precipitants considered: possible stress, dehydration; family history of migraine (mother, sister).
- Medications tried: Ibuprofen 3 tablets/day (dose unspecified) with poor relief.
- Impression: Likely migraine-type headache.

Issue 2:
- Family history of migraine (mother severe with seasonal trigger; sister mild).
- Counseled regarding hereditary component and potential need for prophylaxis if episodes recur.

Issue 3:
- Visual health: longstanding glasses use, no recent optometry review; advised to consider eye test if visual strain persists.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen (self-administered; dose/route/frequency not documented, approx. 3 tablets daily).
- Plan to prescribe Naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented) ± Paracetamol or Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.

Social History:
- Lives with three housemates.
- Works in IT; prolonged screen exposure.
- Social smoker; social alcohol use.
- Mild work stress due to new project.

Preventative History:
- No information on cervical screening, vaccinations, or other preventive care provided.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals or physical exam findings documented (telehealth consult).

Plan:
- Educate on correct ibuprofen dosing (up to 400 mg two tablets three times daily).
- Provide prescription for Naproxen; consider adjunct Paracetamol or Codeine as needed.
- Advise keeping a headache diary to identify triggers.
- Arrange follow-up in 1–2 weeks; earlier review if headaches worsen, develop focal deficits, visual changes, or systemic symptoms.
- Discuss possibility of prophylactic migraine therapy at next visit if recurrent.
- Encourage adequate hydration, screen-time breaks, stress management, and consider optometry review.

Quality checks (document_quality):

● Missing elements: vitals, neurological examination, exact analgesic doses, comprehensive medication and allergy reconciliation, preventive health status (immunizations, cancer screening).
● Internal conflicts: Patient initially responded “Yeah” then “No” to neck pain/stiffness – conflict noted.
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational noise but clinically adequate.
